```{=html}

     style="display:block;margin:0 auto;width:900px;max-width:100%"

  <text x="520" y="235" text-anchor="middle" font-size="22" font-weight="700" letter-spacing="1" fill="#36393B" font-family="'JetBrains Mono','Fira Code',Consolas,monospace">messages[]</text>
```

## This is not your father's AI

::: {style="font-size: 1.1em;"}
::: {.cards .cards-3}
::: {.card}
[October 2025]{.card-title}

"They just don't work. They don't have enough intelligence ... I feel like the industry is making too big of a jump and is trying to pretend like this is amazing, and it's not. It's slop."
:::

::: {.card .card-blue .fragment}
[January 2026]{.card-title}

"I really am mostly programming in English now, a bit sheepishly telling the LLM what code to write... in words."
:::

::: {.card .fragment}
[February–March 2026]{.card-title}

"It is hard to communicate how much programming has changed due to AI in the last 2 months ... Coding agents basically didn't work before December ... I don't think I've typed like a line of code probably since December."
:::
:::
:::

[Andrej Karpathy: OpenAI co-founder, former Tesla AI chief, now at Anthropic]{.eyebrow}

## Prompting

::: {style="font-size: 1.15em;"}
::: {.cards .cards-3}
::: {.card}
[Say what you want]{.card-title}

Not what to do.
:::

::: {.card .card-blue}
[Ask for the best way (plan) first]{.card-title}

Then tell it to proceed.
:::

::: {.card}
[Ask AI to interrogate you]{.card-title}

Let it decide what it needs to know.
:::

::: {.card .card-blue}
[Beware of tunnel vision]{.card-title}

Ask: is there a better path?
:::

::: {.card}
[Steelman]{.card-title}

"What is the strongest argument against this?"
:::

::: {.card .card-blue}
[Numbers need code]{.card-title}

"Compute this in Python."
:::
:::
:::

## New student deliverables

::: {style="font-size: 1.4em; margin-top: 0.6em; line-height: 1.45;"}
- Software apps
- Skills
- Custom agents
:::

## Vibe coding

::: {style="font-size: 1.6em; margin-top: 0.6em; line-height: 1.5;"}
- Students can submit software in addition to spreadsheets.
- Artifacts: single-page HTML apps. Claude can create and deploy.
- More complex software (with backend server). They can run locally or deploy in the cloud or company servers.
- Example: [Tangency portfolio](https://tangency.kerryback.com)
:::

## Agent skills

::: {style="font-size: 1.4em; margin-top: 0.6em; line-height: 1.45;"}
- A skill is a text file of custom instructions for a particular task.
- It can be accompanied by code, including software programs that the agent launches and interacts with.
- Use Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini with custom instructions and software tools in lieu of a custom agent.
- Interaction is via the usual prompt window.
:::

## Plugins

::: {style="font-size: 1.4em; margin-top: 0.6em; line-height: 1.45;"}
- Mechanism for distributing skills.
- In Claude desktop: Customize → Plugins → Add marketplace.
- Anthropic's plugin library: [github.com/anthropics/claude-plugins-official](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-plugins-official)
- kerryback-public plugin library: [github.com/kerryback/kerryback-public](https://github.com/kerryback/kerryback-public)
:::

## MCP servers (connectors)

::: {style="font-size: 1.4em; margin-top: 0.6em; line-height: 1.45;"}
- An MCP server sits between an agent and an external service or database.
- It uses the external service's API and creates tools (functions) from them, which it describes in text form to a connected agent.
- The agent acquires the tools exposed by the server, so it can use the external service.
- Examples: Gmail, Microsoft 365, Slack, Workday, Salesforce, ...
:::

## Custom agents

::: {style="font-size: 1.4em; margin-top: 0.6em; line-height: 1.45;"}
- Custom chatbots with custom tools making API calls.
- Easy to build with agent software development kits (SDKs): code that implements Claude Code or Codex or ...
- Students can build them around class concepts.
- Example of an agent built with a two-line prompt: [[eia-agent.kerryback.com](https://eia-agent.kerryback.com)]{style="white-space: nowrap;"}
:::

## Example exercises

::: {.steps style="font-size: 1.25em; line-height: 1.45;"}
1. Build a dashboard (app) that uses the EIA's API and shows trends in energy prices and volumes.
2. Connect Claude (or Codex, ...) to an EIA MCP server (e.g., eia.kerryback.com/mcp). Create a skill that produces particular plots of energy prices and volumes when invoked.
3. Install the finance-data plugin from the kerryback-public library. Get 60 months of WMT returns using Yahoo Finance data and get MKT-RF and RF from French's data library for the same 60 months. Run the CAPM regression to estimate WMT's beta.
:::

## A skill for DCFs

::: {style="font-size: 1.3em; margin-top: 0.4em; line-height: 1.45;"}
- Instead of creating DCFs, students should create skills or custom agents for creating DCFs.
- Example: `/mydcf {ticker}` gets statements, 10-Ks, press releases, and call transcripts. It writes a page with each judgment call flagged, and a workbook with live formulas.
:::

## Teaching students to check AI work

::: {.cards .cards-2}
::: {.card .card-blue}
[Have AI explain its work]{.card-title}

"Explain what you did step by step. Did you make any decisions that we have not discussed?"
:::

::: {.card}
[Use another AI agent to check the work]{.card-title}

A fresh conversation or a subagent (a second agent that the first agent starts), given your goals and the first agent's explanation.
:::

::: {.card}
[Have AI build a spreadsheet when possible]{.card-title}

Then check the formulas. Every number traces back to its inputs.
:::

::: {.card .card-blue}
[Run the same code on small examples]{.card-title}

Ask AI to run its code on a few rows you can check by hand.
:::
:::

::: {.note}
Most AI coding errors arise from misunderstandings and unstated assumptions --- and from errors that people also make, for example, merging and filtering in the wrong order.
:::

## A separate course {.shrink}

| Part | Topics |
|---|---|
| Models and agents | How language models work; performance; agents; computer use |
| Working with AI | Doing work with AI; prompting; permissions |
| Standing instructions and connectors | CLAUDE.md; memory; SKILL.md; MCP; plugins |
| Building agents | How software works; API calls; a chatbot; an agent |
| Deploying agents | Running locally; Git and GitHub; deployment |
| Documents and local models | RAG; Gemini Notebook; local models |
| Agent security | Multi-agent architectures; risks; mitigation |

[MGMT 803, Gen AI for Business, Rice, four days, September 24–27, 2026. Graded on in-class exercises, screen shares, and participation. The class marketplace holds 28 plugins.]{.eyebrow}
